en.greeting: Hi! At B1 you learnt the words for getting a job. Today it's the job itself: meetings and deadlines, the money side of a business, and who does what in a company.

steps.title: Before, during and after a meeting
steps.text: You already know **meeting**, **deadline** and **colleague**. Let's follow one meeting from start to finish.
steps.body:
- **Before:** the **agenda** = the list of topics. You **brief** someone = give them the key facts before they start.
- **During:** you **discuss** the topics, and someone **takes the minutes** (the written record: always *-s*, nothing to do with time).
- **At the end:** **action points** = tasks with a name and a deadline.
- **After:** you **follow up** on them.

Trap: *membahas tentang* → `discuss about` ✗. **discuss** takes the topic directly: *discuss the budget*. But *talk about* is right.

pairs.en: follow up on the action points

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Hasan runs a small startup in Jakarta. He's planning tomorrow's team meeting.

question.prompt: Pak Hasan: "Tomorrow we need to ___ the new KPI targets."
question.explanation: **discuss** takes the topic directly: *discuss the new KPI targets*. 'discuss about' comes from *membahas tentang*. 'talk' needs *about* here: *talk about the targets*.

steps.title: Projects: on track or behind?
steps.text: Now the words for a project and how it's going.
steps.body:
**Stakeholders** care about the result (client, manager, users). **Milestones** are the big steps on the way. **Deliverables** are what you hand over (a report, an app).

How's it going? **on track / on schedule** (sesuai jadwal), **behind schedule** (terlambat), **ahead of schedule** (lebih cepat). You **meet** or **miss** a deadline.

**postpone** = move to later (*ditunda, diundur*); **cancel** = it won't happen (*dibatalkan*). Schedule: British 'SHED-yool', American 'SKED-jool'.

steps.title: How's the project going?
steps.text: Sari is writing a status update for the stakeholders of a new app.

question.prompt: "We planned to launch the app on 1 March, but the developers need two more weeks." The project is ___.
question.explanation: The app will be two weeks late, so the project is **behind schedule** (terlambat dari jadwal). **on track** means it's going as planned, and **ahead of schedule** means early.

steps.title: Money: revenue − costs = profit
steps.text: Now the money side. One sum explains most of the words.
steps.body:
**revenue** (pendapatan, omzet: all the money from sales) − **costs** (biaya) = **profit** (laba). Costs bigger than revenue: a **loss** (rugi). The same: you **break even** (impas; past *broke even*).

Trap: *mendapat untung* → **make a profit**, not 'get a profit'.

Also: **budget** (anggaran), **invoice** (tagihan), **Q1** (first quarter = three months), **increase by 10%** (naik sebesar 10%). For a person's money, say *income* (penghasilan); for a company's sales, *revenue*.

pairs.id: Penjualan naik sebesar 15% di kuartal kedua.

steps.title: Read the numbers
steps.text: The owner of an online batik shop in Solo is talking about the year.

question.prompt: "This year our sales brought in Rp2 billion. After salaries, rent and ads, Rp300 million was left." What is the Rp2 billion?
question.explanation: All the money that comes in from sales is the **revenue** (Rp2 billion). The **profit** is what's left after the costs (Rp300 million). A **budget** is money you plan to spend.

steps.title: Who does what at work
steps.text: Last group: the people and the structure of a company.
steps.body:
A company has **departments** (Indonesian offices say *divisi*), each with a **head of** department. A **team lead** (British: team leader) runs a small team.

- **report to** someone = that person is your boss.
- **be responsible for** your work or team (bertanggung jawab atas), not 'responsible to'. **be in charge of** means almost the same.
- **colleague** = someone in your own organisation; **counterpart** = someone with the same job as you in **another** organisation.

pairs.en: be in charge of the project

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina works in the finance department of a bank in Jakarta.

question.prompt: Every week Rina has a call with Mr Tan. He does the same job as Rina, but at a partner bank in Singapore. Mr Tan is Rina's ___.
question.explanation: Someone with the **same job** as you in **another organisation** is your **counterpart** (mitra sejawat). A team lead or a head of department would be Rina's boss, in her own bank.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now say what you look after at work. Remember the little word after responsible.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saya bertanggung jawab atas tim penjualan.
question.solution: I am responsible for the sales team.
question.explanation: *bertanggung jawab atas* = **be responsible for** + the work or the people you look after. 'responsible to' is the common mistake.

steps.title: Flashcards
steps.text: Quick review: try to say the English before you flip the card.

flashcards.back: make a profit / make a loss / break even

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Two British Council pages: an article on running good meetings (agenda, minutes, action points in a real text) and a B2 listening where a manager talks about her staff.

id.greeting: Halo! Di B1 kamu sudah belajar kata-kata untuk mencari kerja. Hari ini tentang pekerjaannya sendiri: rapat dan tenggat, sisi keuangan bisnis, dan siapa melakukan apa di perusahaan.

steps.title: Sebelum, selama dan sesudah rapat
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu **meeting**, **deadline** dan **colleague**. Ayo ikuti satu rapat dari awal sampai akhir.
steps.body:
- **Sebelum:** **agenda** = daftar topiknya. Kamu **brief** seseorang = memberi info pentingnya sebelum dia mulai.
- **Selama:** kamu **discuss** topiknya, dan seseorang **takes the minutes** (mencatat notulen: selalu pakai *-s*, tidak ada hubungannya dengan menit).
- **Di akhir:** **action points** = tugas dengan nama orang dan tenggatnya.
- **Sesudahnya:** kamu **follow up** (menindaklanjuti).

Jebakan: *membahas tentang* → `discuss about` ✗. **discuss** langsung diikuti topiknya: *discuss the budget*. Tapi *talk about* benar.

pairs.en: follow up on the action points

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pak Hasan menjalankan startup kecil di Jakarta. Dia sedang menyiapkan rapat tim besok.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Hasan: "Tomorrow we need to ___ the new KPI targets."
question.explanation: **discuss** langsung diikuti topiknya: *discuss the new KPI targets*. 'discuss about' berasal dari *membahas tentang*. 'talk' di sini butuh *about*: *talk about the targets*.

steps.title: Proyek: sesuai jadwal atau terlambat?
steps.text: Sekarang kata-kata untuk proyek dan perkembangannya.
steps.body:
**Stakeholders** peduli pada hasilnya (klien, manajer, pengguna). **Milestones** adalah langkah-langkah besar di perjalanannya. **Deliverables** adalah yang kamu serahkan (laporan, aplikasi).

Bagaimana perkembangannya? **on track / on schedule** (sesuai jadwal), **behind schedule** (terlambat), **ahead of schedule** (lebih cepat). Kamu **meet** atau **miss** a deadline.

**postpone** = dipindah ke nanti (*ditunda, diundur*); **cancel** = tidak jadi (*dibatalkan*). Schedule: British 'SYED-yuul', Amerika 'SKED-juul'.

steps.title: Bagaimana proyeknya?
steps.text: Sari sedang menulis laporan perkembangan untuk para pemangku kepentingan sebuah aplikasi baru.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: "We planned to launch the app on 1 March, but the developers need two more weeks." The project is ___.
question.explanation: Aplikasinya akan terlambat dua minggu, jadi proyeknya **behind schedule** (terlambat dari jadwal). **on track** berarti berjalan sesuai rencana, dan **ahead of schedule** berarti lebih cepat.

steps.title: Uang: revenue − costs = profit
steps.text: Sekarang sisi keuangannya. Satu rumus menjelaskan sebagian besar katanya.
steps.body:
**revenue** (pendapatan, omzet: semua uang dari penjualan) − **costs** (biaya) = **profit** (laba). Biaya lebih besar dari pendapatan: **loss** (rugi). Sama besar: kamu **break even** (impas; lampaunya *broke even*).

Jebakan: *mendapat untung* → **make a profit**, bukan 'get a profit'.

Juga: **budget** (anggaran), **invoice** (tagihan), **Q1** (kuartal pertama = tiga bulan), **increase by 10%** (naik sebesar 10%). Untuk uang seseorang, pakai *income* (penghasilan); untuk penjualan perusahaan, *revenue*.

pairs.id: Penjualan naik sebesar 15% di kuartal kedua.

steps.title: Baca angkanya
steps.text: Pemilik toko batik online di Solo sedang bercerita tentang tahun ini.

question.prompt: "This year our sales brought in Rp2 billion. After salaries, rent and ads, Rp300 million was left." Rp2 miliar itu apa?
question.explanation: Semua uang yang masuk dari penjualan adalah **revenue** (Rp2 miliar). **Profit** adalah sisanya setelah biaya (Rp300 juta). **Budget** adalah uang yang kamu rencanakan untuk dibelanjakan.

steps.title: Siapa melakukan apa di kantor
steps.text: Kelompok terakhir: orang-orang dan struktur perusahaan.
steps.body:
Perusahaan punya **departments** (di kantor Indonesia sering disebut *divisi*), masing-masing dengan **head of** department (kepala). **Team lead** (British: team leader) memimpin tim kecil.

- **report to** seseorang = orang itu atasanmu.
- **be responsible for** pekerjaan atau timmu (bertanggung jawab atas), bukan 'responsible to'. **be in charge of** artinya hampir sama.
- **colleague** = orang di organisasimu sendiri; **counterpart** = orang dengan pekerjaan yang sama di organisasi **lain**.

pairs.en: be in charge of the project

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina bekerja di departemen keuangan sebuah bank di Jakarta.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Every week Rina has a call with Mr Tan. He does the same job as Rina, but at a partner bank in Singapore. Mr Tan is Rina's ___.
question.explanation: Orang dengan **pekerjaan yang sama** denganmu di **organisasi lain** adalah **counterpart** (mitra sejawat). Team lead atau head of department adalah atasan Rina, di banknya sendiri.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang katakan apa yang kamu urus di kantor. Ingat kata kecil setelah responsible.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Saya bertanggung jawab atas tim penjualan.
question.solution: I am responsible for the sales team.
question.explanation: *bertanggung jawab atas* = **be responsible for** + pekerjaan atau orang yang kamu urus. 'responsible to' adalah kesalahan yang umum.
